name: Secure the Mountain

angles.text: Dun Morogh is the ancestral mountain home of the Bronzebeard dwarves. Mountaineer Gretchen's stubborn vigil helps protect her kin from the dangers around them.
Safe high passes around Ironforge matter to travel and defense across the Alliance's snowy stronghold in Khaz Modan.

faq.answer: Mountaineer Gretchen is an Ironforge sentry in Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness. After a deadly scouting effort in a nearby cave, she writes a field report on the hostile creatures and sends it to Kharanos. She remains at her post until the surrounding territory is secure.

Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven authority in Kharanos. He coordinates local security across Dun Morogh and receives dispatches and scouting assessments from mountaineers in the field. He catalogs the reports to assess threats across the region.

Cornelius was a fellow scout who explored the infested cavern. He died in the failed scouting effort, and Mountaineer Gretchen speaks of his loss with regret. His death helped convince her the cave was a deadly trap and no more scouts should enter.

aliases: why is the cave a death trap
faq.answer: Scouts found the mountain cavern overrun by hostile mongrels, and Cornelius died in the effort. Mountaineer Gretchen judged the tunnels a lost cause and refused to risk more scouts there. She chose to avoid the area.
faq.q: What happened in the mountain cave?

faq.answer: Mountaineer Gretchen says she will not abandon her post until the mountain is secure. Though the nearby cavern is too dangerous to retake, she stays on the snowy heights to watch the approach and sends word of the threat to Kharanos.
faq.q: Why does Gretchen refuse to leave her post?

faq.answer: Senir Whitebeard is hardly surprised to hear the cavern is overrun. He accepts the news and adds Gretchen's dispatch to his growing stack of notes, keeping a careful record of the dangers facing the realm.
faq.q: How does Senir Whitebeard react to Gretchen's report?

faq.answer: Mountaineers are Ironforge's frontier scouts and border guards in Dun Morogh. These hardy dwarves patrol snowy peaks, high trails and passes, watch for hostile beasts, explore caverns, and report dangers to places like Kharanos. Their work protects travelers and settlements.
faq.q: What role do the Mountaineers play in Dun Morogh?

sections.body: Mountaineer Gretchen watches Dun Morogh's high passes from her post in the freezing peaks. A recent venture into a nearby cavern showed her how dangerous the wilderness remains. Hostile mongrels overrun its tunnels, and she judges the cave a death trap. Gretchen will risk no more lives there. She holds the line on the slopes and sends an emissary with her written assessment.
sections.title: A Grim Report

sections.body: Cornelius was among those lost in the failed scouting effort, and his death weighs heavily on Mountaineer Gretchen. She admits the cavern cannot be reclaimed under current conditions, so she halts further exploration of its tunnels. Her concern now is holding the threat back. She will sacrifice no more scouts to the creatures beneath the snowy crags.
sections.title: Losses in the Depths

sections.body: From Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard tracks dangers to the dwarven heartland. Gretchen's report brings little surprise: the cavern is overrun. He adds her letter to his growing stack of field reports. Each account helps Ironforge record and manage the dangers along its frontier.
sections.title: Senir Whitebeard's Dossier

summary: Mountaineer Gretchen sends a grim report from Dun Morogh to Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. Scouts have found a nearby cave overrun, and she will risk no more lives in its tunnels. Ironforge must still guard the mountain frontier from rising threats.
